data.summary: Microscopist on 4 field(s): density similar vs DMSO; 6 observations; candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors

observations.finding: Treated fields (f_e49f75311a04, f_3d278fa72a10 at 1.0 uM, 364 cells; f_169783cedcc2, f_dd8e8b1b5262 at 10.0 uM, 210 cells) are markedly less confluent than DMSO control f_9fbcadfb9d0d. DMSO shows dense monolayer of mononucleate cells with round-oval blue nuclei and filamentous green tubulin. Treated fields show scattered single cells and small clusters.

DAPI-blue nuclei in treated vs DMSO: markedly irregular, lobed, C-shaped and elongated rather than round-oval. Nuclear contour shows indentations and bi/multi-lobed appearance in many cells, read from blue channel in composite at identical contrast. Phenotype present at 1.0 uM and more severe at 10.0 uM.

Reduced nuclear form factor (0.848 at 1uM, 0.831 at 10uM vs DMSO median 0.917, z -38.5/-47.9) = loss of circularity; reduced solidity (0.958/0.949 vs 0.972, z -35.7/-57.2) = indentations/lobulation; increased eccentricity (0.689/0.711 vs 0.601, z +13.9/+17.5) = elongation. All visible as irregular/lobed eccentric nuclei in composite.

Increased fraction of cells with >1 nuclear lobe/nucleus per cell. Composite shows frequent binucleate and multilobed nuclei (two or more blue masses within one green/red cytoplasm) vs rare in DMSO. Measured frac_multinucleate_proxy 0.644/0.609 vs DMSO 0.268, z +17.5/+15.9, consistent.

F-actin red channel in composite: brighter and more heterogeneous/patchy cortical signal in treated vs thin cortical red in DMSO. Peripheral ruffles and variable intensity across cells, with higher contrast texture. Measured act_mean 0.512/0.563 vs 0.293 z +14.7/+18.1; act_std 0.161/0.183 vs 0.072 z +19.7/+24.5; act_glcm_contrast 0.004 vs 0.001 z +21.6/+27.6, consistent with brighter, more variable, higher-contrast actin. Seen only via red in composite, no separate grayscale.

Beta-tubulin green channel: filamentous microtubules still present, no global loss, but texture more heterogeneous/high-contrast vs DMSO lacy green mesh. No monopolar rosettes or collapsed microtubule bundles visible in composite. Measured tub_glcm_contrast 0.006 vs 0.002 z +14.4/+16.0, consistent with increased texture contrast.

notable_cells.why: cluster of cells with binucleate/multilobed blue nuclei illustrating reduced solidity/form factor and multinucleate proxy
elongated bi-lobed nucleus with bright patchy red cortical actin illustrating increased eccentricity and act_mean/std/contrast
binucleate cell with irregular DAPI lobes and green tubulin heterogeneity illustrating strongest solidity loss at 10uM z-57

candidate_mechanisms.why: Combination of cytokinesis-failure phenotype: very large decreases in nuc_form_factor/solidity, increased nuc_eccentricity, and ~2.3x increase in multinucleate proxy, with retained microtubules and enhanced cortical actin heterogeneity/brightness, matches Aurora B cytokinesis failure/polyploidy, not microtubule loss/stabilization or actin depolymerization alone. Same phenotype at 1uM and stronger at 10uM. Other MoAs on list do not produce this degree of multinucleation with actin/tubulin contrast increase.

report.uncertainty: Only composites provided, 1024x819 px, so DAPI/tubulin/actin read from blue/green/red color at identical contrast; fine filament detail limited. No Eg5 monopolar spindles or microtubule depolymerization/bundling seen, arguing against Eg5 inhibitors or Microtubule destabilizers/stabilizers. DNA damage/replication could alter nuclear shape but would not explain act_mean/std and tub_contrast increases plus very high multinucleate fraction.

reflection.text:
Unblinding: compound was **emetine** (PubChem CID 10219, name/BBBC021 structure agree, e23-e24) and truth MoA is **Protein synthesis**, not Aurora. Verdict incorrect - I remained on Aurora kinase inhibitors (p=0.72 -> p=0.45).

**What the data actually got right:**

The strongest signal in favor of the truth was already present in e5 **compare_to_reference_atlas**: 5/10 nearest neighbours Protein synthesis and 3/10 Microtubule destabilizers at mean similarity 0.91/0.88, with no Aurora neighbours. This directly contradicted my call. The dose_response panel also contradicted the Aurora cytokinesis-failure model I invoked in e16: frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=+0.40 p=0.6 not monotonic (e9), frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.60 p=0.4 (e12), cell_count rho=+0.80 p=0.2 with no dose-dependent loss (e10), nuc_area rho=-0.40 p=0.6 with no increase (e14), frac_large_nucleus rho=+0.40 p=0.6 (e20), tub_mean rho=-0.80 p=0.2 decreasing rather than retained (e13). For Aurora B failure I predicted polyploid enlargement and mitotic accumulation with retained microtubules; none of those monotonic trends were significant. My second hypothesis update e21 correctly raised Protein synthesis to 0.30 based on e5+e10+e13+e14, acknowledging the atlas, but still underweighted it.

Literature found in this run supports the unblinded truth that emetine is a protein synthesis inhibitor: PMID 4347870 and PMID 191850 returned for `emetine protein synthesis inhibitor mechanism`. ChEMBL had no curated mechanism (e23), so atlas + literature should have outweighed morphology.

**What misled me and why:**

1. Extreme nuclear shape metrics dominated reasoning: nuc_form_factor z=-29.6 to -47.9 and nuc_solidity z=-30.4 to -57.2 at 0.1-10 µM (e2,e3,e6,e7) with perfect monotonic loss rho=-1.00 p=0 (e8,e18) plus high act_glcm_contrast z=+21.6 to +27.6. I interpreted lobulation/irregularity + heterogeneous actin as Aurora cytokinesis failure. In retrospect this was a magnitude fallacy without a dose anchor.

2. e4 **describe_phenotype**: microscopist on 4 fields, density similar vs DMSO, with candidate list `Aurora kinase inhibitors`. Single-well visual impression with no quantitative multinucleation threshold and no pHH3/DNA-content data was overweighted in e15 (supporting e2,e3,e4,e6,e7,e8,e9) vs single contradicting e5.

3. Acquisition strategy caused saturation blindness. From e1 (8 doses 0.01-30 µM, 4/4 wells available) I sampled 1 µM (e2), 10 µM (e3), then 0.1 µM (e6) and 3 µM (e7). All four points were already saturated for the key discriminators: review correctly noted cell count, actin and multinucleation saturated at 0.1 µM, and mean nuclear area did not increase as expected for polyploidy while marked cell shrinkage (e17 cell_area rho=-0.40) could artifactually elevate actin/tubulin intensities. With n=4 and most dose_response p=0.2-0.8, only form_factor/solidity was truly dose-responsive; I over-interpreted non-significant trends as supportive.

No DMSO control well and no sub-saturating dose (0.03 µM dose index 1 or 0.01 µM) were acquired. That made the test the reviewer requested - Aurora should show form-factor/multinucleation loss *before* cell-area/count collapse, while protein-synthesis/generic shrinkage should track together - impossible. I spent the 4-well budget (e1) before the critique (review verdict request_experiment) and then submitted e22 at p=0.45 with rationale `cannot acquire... budget spent... saturation already at 0.1 µM`. Over-calibration from 0.72 to 0.45 still ignored that 5/10 atlas neighbours + lack of polyploidy growth should have made Protein synthesis the leading hypothesis.

**Why I missed it:**

I treated atlas similarity as noisy and treated single-replicate extreme z-scores as specific, rather than recognizing nuclear irregularity can be secondary to translation arrest, cell shrinkage and actin remodeling. I did not heed that in protein synthesis inhibition, cytoskeletal heterogeneity and lobulation can occur without true cytokinesis failure, and that my own metrics (no nuc_area increase, no significant multinucleation dose trend, tub_mean decline) falsified the specific Aurora prediction.

Correct next step was the requested low-dose acquisition plus orthogonal readouts I listed in e16/e22 but never executed: p-Histone H3 Ser10, p-Aurora T232/T288 IF and DNA-content flow for 8N polyploidy vs cycloheximide and microtubule controls. Future runs should reserve budget for DMSO and 0.01-0.03 µM anchors before sampling high doses, and weight atlas consensus over single-well morphology when n=4 and p>0.2.

This is a cell-biology screening reflection only, not clinical advice.

The strongest signal in favor of the truth was already present in e5 **compare_to_reference_atlas**: 5/10 nearest neighbours Protein synthesis and 3/10 Microtubule destabilizers at mean similarity 0.91/0.88, with no Aurora neighbours. This directly contradicted my call. The dose_response panel also contradicted the Aurora cytokinesis-failure model I invoked in e16: frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=+0.40 p=0.6 not monotonic (e9), frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.60 p=0.4 (e12), cell_count rho=+0.80 p=0.2 with no dose-dependent loss (e10), nuc_area rho=-0.40 p=0.6 with no increase (e14), frac_large_nucleus rho=+0.40 p=0.6 (e20), tub_mean rho=-0.80 p=0.2 decreasing rather than retained (e13). For Aurora B failure I predicted polyploid enlargement and mitotic accumulation with retained microtubules; none of those monotonic trends were significant. My second hypothesis update e21 correctly raised Protein synthesis to 0.30 based on e5+e10+e13+e14, acknowledging the atlas, but still underweighted it.

Literature found in this run supports the unblinded truth that emetine is a protein synthesis inhibitor: PMID 4347870 and PMID 191850 returned for `emetine protein synthesis inhibitor mechanism`. ChEMBL had no curated mechanism (e23), so atlas + literature should have outweighed morphology.

**What misled me and why:**

1. Extreme nuclear shape metrics dominated reasoning: nuc_form_factor z=-29.6 to -47.9 and nuc_solidity z=-30.4 to -57.2 at 0.1-10 µM (e2,e3,e6,e7) with perfect monotonic loss rho=-1.00 p=0 (e8,e18) plus high act_glcm_contrast z=+21.6 to +27.6. I interpreted lobulation/irregularity + heterogeneous actin as Aurora cytokinesis failure. In retrospect this was a magnitude fallacy without a dose anchor.

2. e4 **describe_phenotype**: microscopist on 4 fields, density similar vs DMSO, with candidate list `Aurora kinase inhibitors`. Single-well visual impression with no quantitative multinucleation threshold and no pHH3/DNA-content data was overweighted in e15 (supporting e2,e3,e4,e6,e7,e8,e9) vs single contradicting e5.

3. Acquisition strategy caused saturation blindness. From e1 (8 doses 0.01-30 µM, 4/4 wells available) I sampled 1 µM (e2), 10 µM (e3), then 0.1 µM (e6) and 3 µM (e7). All four points were already saturated for the key discriminators: review correctly noted cell count, actin and multinucleation saturated at 0.1 µM, and mean nuclear area did not increase as expected for polyploidy while marked cell shrinkage (e17 cell_area rho=-0.40) could artifactually elevate actin/tubulin intensities. With n=4 and most dose_response p=0.2-0.8, only form_factor/solidity was truly dose-responsive; I over-interpreted non-significant trends as supportive.

No DMSO control well and no sub-saturating dose (0.03 µM dose index 1 or 0.01 µM) were acquired. That made the test the reviewer requested - Aurora should show form-factor/multinucleation loss *before* cell-area/count collapse, while protein-synthesis/generic shrinkage should track together - impossible. I spent the 4-well budget (e1) before the critique (review verdict request_experiment) and then submitted e22 at p=0.45 with rationale `cannot acquire... budget spent... saturation already at 0.1 µM`. Over-calibration from 0.72 to 0.45 still ignored that 5/10 atlas neighbours + lack of polyploidy growth should have made Protein synthesis the leading hypothesis.

**Why I missed it:**

I treated atlas similarity as noisy and treated single-replicate extreme z-scores as specific, rather than recognizing nuclear irregularity can be secondary to translation arrest, cell shrinkage and actin remodeling. I did not heed that in protein synthesis inhibition, cytoskeletal heterogeneity and lobulation can occur without true cytokinesis failure, and that my own metrics (no nuc_area increase, no significant multinucleation dose trend, tub_mean decline) falsified the specific Aurora prediction.

Correct next step was the requested low-dose acquisition plus orthogonal readouts I listed in e16/e22 but never executed: p-Histone H3 Ser10, p-Aurora T232/T288 IF and DNA-content flow for 8N polyploidy vs cycloheximide and microtubule controls. Future runs should reserve budget for DMSO and 0.01-0.03 µM anchors before sampling high doses, and weight atlas consensus over single-well morphology when n=4 and p>0.2.

This is a cell-biology screening reflection only, not clinical advice.
